# The radius of a BallVector of one limb times a number of T

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `bv_scale_radius_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

Numbers of `T` that bound expressions of $m, r_x, a$ from above:

$$r_z \ge \lvert a\rvert r_x + \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})} + \frac{\mathrm{tiny}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})}.$$

## C++

No public operation computes this kernel on its own. It is part of the loop `bv_scale_1`, called by `x * a`, `a * x`, `x *= a`, `scale(x, a, z)` and `axpy` of `BallVector<T, 1, N>` and `BallVectorView<T, 1>` ([Ball vectors](ball_vector.md)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.
- $m \ge 0$.
- $r_x \ge 0$.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $r_z \ge \lvert a\rvert r_x + \frac{m \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})} + \frac{\mathrm{tiny}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})}{1 - \mathrm{unit}(\mathtt{mul\_1\_1})}$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `bv_scale_radius_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/BvRadius.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/BvRadius.v), against `bv_scale_radius_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions bv_scale_radius_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition bv_scale_radius_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall m rx a : R,
  fmt emin prec m ->
  fmt emin prec rx ->
  fmt emin prec a ->
  0 <= m ->
  0 <= rx ->
  let rz := bv_scale_radius_1 emin prec tie_even m rx a in
  fmt emin prec rz /\
  ((((Rabs a) * rx) + ((m * ((1 / (1 + u prec)) * u prec ^ 1)) / (1 - ((1 / (1 + u prec)) * u prec ^ 1)))) + (((1 / 2) * eta emin) / (1 - ((1 / (1 + u prec)) * u prec ^ 1)))) <= rz.
```

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

## Source

**Algorithm:** the radius lines of ball_scale_1 (Milestone 1, second radius design), at the largest magnitude of a center of the result (milestone2.md, BallVector). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/bv_scale_radius_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/bv_scale_radius_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# The one radius of a BallVector with one-limb centers times a number a of T (milestone2.md,
# "BallVector": bv_scale_radius_k): the radius lines of ball_scale_1, with m, the largest magnitude
# of a center of the result, in place of one entry's |cz|. Every operation is a rounding of a
# nondecreasing function of m on nonnegative values, so with m the largest |cz| the result is the
# largest of the radii that ball_scale_1 returns entry by entry. Its claim is what makes it a radius
# of every entry: by the bound of mul_1_1 relative to the result, an entry whose exact center is
# s = cx a and computed center cz has |cz - s| <= U |cz| + T <= U m + T, with U = unit/(1 - unit)
# and T = tiny/(1 - unit), and a member x a of the exact product is within |a| rx of s. The program
# gives a (an entry kernel): it is only multiplied, after its magnitude.

aa = abs(a)
p  = prod(aa, rx)
t  = fma(m, const up(unit(mul_1_1)/(1-unit(mul_1_1))), p)
rz = fma(t, const up((1+u)^3), const up((1+u)*((1+u)^2*eta+tiny(mul_1_1)/(1-unit(mul_1_1))+eta/2)+eta/(2*u)))
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#bv_scale_radius_1)).

**These runs judged other claims.** They judged `upper(rz) >= abs(a)*rx+m*unit(mul_1_1)/(1-unit(mul_1_1))+tiny(mul_1_1)/(1-unit(mul_1_1))`; the kernel now claims `upper(rz) abs(a)*rx+m*unit(mul_1_1)/(1-unit(mul_1_1))+tiny(mul_1_1)/(1-unit(mul_1_1))`. Their numbers are not about the statement above.

| Run | Cases judged | Failed | largest excess, in gaps | Bound attained |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 | - | - |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 | - | - |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 3 958 812 | 0 | - | - |

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
